critical_code_review_comments: useLiveAuctions.js: `const base = ...` with subsequent `q = q.eq(...)` chains was a broken refactor of the previous `let q = ...` pattern. It escaped review because unit tests / lint on changed file was not run. Recommend enabling ESLint `no-undef` and running lint on modified files in CI.

rca of the issue: useLiveAuctions.js was refactored to add the `category=='collectibles'` -> `auction_type=='NFT'` filter and a keyword search branch. During that refactor, the initial query builder was renamed from `let q = ...` to `const base = ...`, but every subsequent branch still referenced `q`. Because the module is ES-strict, assignments to the undeclared `q` throw ReferenceError inside the queryFn; React Query reports isError=true on the initial load and, on subsequent refetches with different params, transiently isLoading=true, which explains the skeleton I saw with category=collectibles. Reproduction: (a) unauth or auth, visit /?tab=all; before fix -> live-auctions-error banner; (b) visit /?category=collectibles&tab=all; before fix -> permanent skeleton. Mitigation: renamed `const base` to `let q` (single-line change) so every existing branch works as originally intended. Recommend adding ESLint `no-undef` to prevent this class of bug.
